notes: 2 plates of 384 wells for 43 samples, each in 2 replicates per assay.
Every repeated sample is run with the reference genes (ALUsq(Eurogentec), HMBS, HPRT1, SDHA(1), UBC(2)) on its own plate, so it is normalised within the plate.
Every plate carries, for every assay on it, the inter-run calibrator 1842 in 2 replicates: a sample of the original run, so the repeat can be put on the scale of the original runs (Hellemans 2007).
Per assay and plate, too: 1 no-RT control well (NRT), 1 no-template control well (NTC).
Samples are dealt to the plates in a random order (seeded); rename the controls in the CSV to your own tubes.
The original run had 1 well(s) per sample and gene; the repeat runs 2, so a single well that is off can be told from the sample.
Suggested inter-run calibrator: sample 1842 (compared in this study, a value for every repeated gene, nothing points at it); any sample of the original plates works.
110 item(s) change no call: they are listed but not on the plate (put every item on it to re-run them too).
2 item(s) point at a sample's tube, not a well: check the tube first (input, extraction); the plate carries it only for the calls it changes.

note: What the checks point at, per sample and gene, most consequential first: the Run Gate's warnings and failures, the wells a person left out, samples in no comparison, wells with no amplification where the gene amplified in nearly every other sample, and Trace's places to look. Re-running is your call: the plan changes nothing in the analysis.
